title: Autoregressive networks with dependent edges: consistency of the initial estimator for the global and local parameters
author: Jinyuan Chang, Qin Fang, Eric D. Kolaczyk, Peter W. MacDonald, Qiwei Yao
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 945--947, source label tm:consistency): under the conditions of the article's identification proposition, the initial estimator of the global parameters achieves the stated rate in the Euclidean norm and the initial estimator of the local parameters achieves the stated rate in the supremum norm, both in probability approaching one; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 3163--3227 (the article's own appendix proof subsection of 65 lines, whose heading names the counted theorem and whose argument ends with the article's completion sentence and end-of-proof symbol). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context. It first records the two rates and the uniform-covariance lemma that it states inside the proof and then uses, obtains a uniform deviation bound for the estimated logistic-type criterion over the parameter space, converts the identification lower bound of the retained proposition into a sharp quadratic lower bound for the criterion near the truth, compares the two to force the deviation to be small with probability approaching one, and deduces the supremum-norm rate for the local parameters by a further exponential-tail argument; the auxiliary lemma quoted by the proof is stated and its role explained inside the same retained span, and its own proof is cited by section reference, which resolves to the retained appendix heading. H2: a research-level consistency theorem for a temporally dependent network model with a diverging number of parameters; the proof combines a martingale-difference uniform deviation bound, a sharp identification inequality and a two-step rate extraction, which is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
